AMPChatMessage.description: These fields are populated by enriching the base chat messages with user info.
AMPChatMessage.title: AMPChatMessage extends ChatMessageQuery with AMP-specific display fields.

heldbyrippling.description:
HeldByRippling is true when this message is CURRENTLY held by the rippling reply-hold
engine (a rippling_held_replies row with status='held'). Populated for moderators (any
message) and for a normal caller on their OWN held reply, so the sender can show a
"waiting to send" indicator. It is NOT set on the poster's view (the delivery gate
removes held replies from their fetch entirely).

Only 'held' counts. 'taken-gone' and 'dropped' are terminal - the reply was never
delivered and never will be - so treating them as "held" told a moderator (and the
sender) that delivery was still coming when it was not. Use RipplingHold to tell the
terminal states apart.

processingfailreason.description:
Processingfailreason says WHY a message was dropped during processing
(processingsuccessful = 0). A dropped message is never notified to the recipient and
is filtered out of their chat fetch, so without this a support volunteer sees a
message the recipient swears never arrived and has no way to explain it - which is
how a run of suppressed replies got put down to a rippling delay. Values come from
ChatMessage::PROCESSFAIL_* in the batch app.

Read-only here (`gorm:"->"`): only the batch processor ever sets it, and without
this GORM adds it to every chat_messages INSERT, which fails outright on a database
that has the code but not yet the migration.

replysource.description:
Replysource is the client-reported surface an Interested reply came from (browse,
search, message_page, notification, ...). Advisory reply-provenance evidence for the
rippling attribution capture - sanitised there, stored in rippling_reply_attribution,
never a chat_messages column.

sensitive.description:
Sensitive is set for the recipient of a message the content check held, when the
warn-not-hold experiment is on (see warnnothold.go). It names the kind of care to take;
the client shows the text behind a warning the member taps through. Never set for
the sender or for a moderator, who see the moderation fields instead.

AMPChatResponse.title: AMPChatResponse wraps the enriched chat messages with AMP-specific metadata.

AdminUser.title: AdminUser is the creator of an admin, as V1 returned it.

BulkItem.description:
A message is a bulk offer when it has rows in messages_bulk_items; the message

BulkItem.title: BulkItem is one catalogue item within a bulk-offer ("clearance") message.

ChatPrompt.title: ChatPrompt is the answerable part of a Prompt message, as served to the client.

expired.description:
Expired prompts still render (the conversation should not develop holes)
but stop offering their buttons.

msgids.description:
Msgids are the posts the question is about and the answer applies to.
Usually several: Freegle talks about a member's outstanding posts together,
the way a clearance treats its items. The client lists them so the subject
is never ambiguous, which is also why the wording names no post.

systemchat.description:
Systemchat marks a chat with the Freegle account rather than with a person.
The client uses it to show a different header: most of what Freegle says is
not a conversation, so rating, blocking or reporting it is nonsense, and
"this is automated" belongs there once instead of on every message.

ClientLogRequest.title: ClientLogRequest represents the request body for client logs.

CommentItem.title: CommentItem is a flat comment representation. Client fetches user details separately via /user/:id.

CountsResponse.title: CountsResponse is the API response for the counts endpoint.

EEELabelChallenge.description:
EEELabelChallenge represents a Freegle item to be labelled for EEE
(Electrical / Electronic Equipment) classification training.

GiftAid.description: GiftAid represents a user's Gift Aid declaration

Group.title: Group represents a Freegle group overlapping with an authority.

HousekeeperTask.title: HousekeeperTask is the DB row returned by ListTasks.

IllustrationData.title: IllustrationData contains the AI illustration details.

IllustrationResult.title: IllustrationResult is the response structure for the illustration endpoint.

LogEntry.title: LogEntry represents a single log entry returned from the API.

LogsResponse.title: LogsResponse is the API response structure.

Map.description: Map is a shortcut for map[string]interface{}, useful for JSON returns

Message.description: Message represents a posting (offer or wanted)

accessinstructions.description:
Accessinstructions is the offerer's private note (address / gate code /
intercom). Only returned to the offerer or a moderator — never to general
viewers — and sent to a replier only once they're promised an item.

approvedby.description:
Approvedby/Approvedat/Rejectedat carry the moderation decision. Approvedby is nil
unless the caller is a moderator (see GetMessagesByIds), for the same reason as
Heldby above: it would otherwise reveal a moderator's identity to a general viewer.

bulkitems.description:
BulkItems is the structured catalogue for a bulk offer ("clearance"). Nil
(and omitted) for ordinary single-item posts. Bulkcount is len(BulkItems),
exposed so list/summary views can flag a bulk offer cheaply.

bulkslots.description: Bulkslots are the offerer-defined collection windows a replier picks from.

collection.description:
Collection is messages.collection: this message's single national moderation state
(Incoming/Pending/Approved/Spam/Rejected). There is no per-group collection any more.

contentcheckcheckedat.description:
ContentcheckCheckedAt/ContentcheckReasons are moderator-only (see GetMessagesByIds):
the reasons name the keyword that flagged the post, which would tell a spammer
exactly what to avoid next time.

heldby.description:
Heldby is messages.heldby directly: a message has one moderation state, not one
per group. nil unless the caller is a moderator (see GetMessagesByIds), so a
held post does not announce that fact to anyone else.

partgone.description:
Partgone is true once somebody has been recorded as having taken some of a
multi-item post. It is a fact about takers, not arithmetic on the two counts
above: an ordinary poster is no longer asked how many each person took, so
availablenow stops tracking reality the moment the first person is recorded.
Bulk offers still count items out one by one and use the numbers instead.

reachesyouat.description:
ReachesYouAt: when this post's rippling reach is expected to arrive at the
viewer, for a post they can see but which has not rippled to them yet. Set only
alongside ReplyEligible=false and only for the reach reason - a viewer blocked
by a ban is not waiting for the ripple, so it stays nil there.

ReachesYouFully says which question was answered. True: a tick of the post's own
schedule grows far enough to include them, and this is when. False: no tick ever
does, so this is instead when the reach stops expanding - the point their held
reply is passed on regardless. Both are real answers; the second is the common
one, and it is an upper bound rather than a prediction, because a reach also
finishes early when the post gathers enough repliers or is taken.

reachfinished.description:
ReachFinished: the post's reach has stopped expanding (rippling_reach.status
'done') without covering the viewer, so it is never going to. Set instead of
ReachesYouAt, whose final-tick date would already be in the past and read as
"any moment now" about a reach that ended weeks ago (Discourse 9808/797). The
reply is still held for the moment and released by the finished-reach sweep.

replyeligible.description:
ReplyEligible: rippling-out (#2). nil/omitted = eligible (the post isn't rippling,
i.e. has no rippling_reach row, or eligibility wasn't computed). false = the post
has rippled out but not yet to the viewer's location, so the UI shows it view-only.

roadmins.description:
Road drive time/distance from the VIEWER's home to this post's blurred
location, filled by one batched routing call per message fetch (nil when
the viewer is logged out, has no location, or the reach engine cannot
answer - clients then show crow-flies). Shipping it with the message
saves the client a /drivedistance round trip per rendered card.

visibleSince.description:
VisibleSince is the earliest this post could have been seen: the oldest arrival across
the groups it is live on. The feed orders by it and the card dates by it, so the list
cannot contradict the dates printed on it.

Arrival above is messages.arrival - when it was first written - which is NOT the same
thing once a post has been reposted or has rippled: this browse view was ordering by
Arrival while the card showed a group arrival, so a 20-day-old post displaying "5 days"
sat above a 3-hour-old one.

MessageAttachment.description:
The ai field is true when the attachment was generated by the Freegle AI illustration service.
Partners (e.g. TrashNothing) can use this to identify and selectively remove AI-generated images.
MessageAttachment.title: MessageAttachment represents an image attached to a message.

MessagePosting.title: MessagePosting represents a posting history record from messages_postings.

MessagePromise.description:
MessagePromise is a row of messages_promises. The Terms/Acceptedat/Acceptedby
fields are the optional "agreement" extension (see handleAcceptAgreement):
they stay NULL - and are omitted from the JSON - unless a client chooses to
use them, so a plain Freegle promise serialises exactly as it always has.

ModFeedbackRequest.description: ModFeedbackRequest represents the body for PATCH /microvolunteering

seenwatermark.description:
The user's newsfeed_users high-water mark, set only on the top-level item
returned by Single() so the client can baseline "new since my last visit"
on any entry path (feed card or notification deep link) without an extra
request. Never populated on nested replies.

NoticeboardItem.title: NoticeboardItem is a flat V2 response. Client fetches user details separately via /user/:id.

Photo.description: Photo represents a photo for rotation challenge

PostRequest.description:
The operation is determined by which fields are present:
externaluid present → create new attachment
id + rotate present → rotate existing attachment
PostRequest.title: PostRequest handles all POST /image operations.

imgtype.description: Type resolution: either imgtype string or boolean flags

PostcodeStats.title: PostcodeStats represents stats for a partial postcode.

action.description:
Action is a hint to the client that answering should also take the member
somewhere, e.g. "editmessage" to open the post editor. Advisory only: the
server records the answer either way.

input.description:
Input marks an option that takes a value from the member rather than being
a fixed choice - currently only "date". The client renders the matching
control and sends what was entered as the answer.

ReplyResponse.title: ReplyResponse is the response for AMP chat reply submissions.

RipplingHold.description:
RipplingHold describes what the rippling reply-hold engine did to a chat message, so a
moderator investigating "they say they never got my reply" can see whether it was delayed,
how long for, and whether it ever arrived at all.

delivered.description:
Delivered is true only for 'released'. 'taken-gone' (the item went while the reply was
held) and 'dropped' never reached the recipient and never will, so the UI must not offer
to wait for them.

heldat.description: Heldat is when the hold was placed, i.e. when the reply was written.

heldminutes.description:
Heldminutes is how long the reply was undelivered: Heldat to Releasedat, or Heldat to now
for a live hold. Computed server-side so a still-open hold does not depend on the
client's clock, and so the client need not know that a NULL releasedat means "until now".

releasedat.description: Releasedat is when the hold ended, whatever the ending. Nil while still held.

status.description: Status is rippling_held_replies.status verbatim: held | released | dropped | taken-gone.

SearchResult.title: SearchResult represents an authority search result.

emailfrequency.description:
A member's email frequency, events/volunteering opt-in, posting status and ban are
site-wide attributes on users now, not per-community memberships rows.

ljuserid.description:
No gorm:"->" — user/auth.go GetLoveJunkUser writes this column via
db.Create(&ljuser) when first creating an LJ-linked user; making it
read-only would silently drop the value and cause a fresh user to be
created on every LJ call (TestCreateChatMessageLoveJunk regression).

redacted.description:
Set when the name, photo and about-me were withheld (see hideTNIdentityFromAnonymous),
so a client that cached this copy before logging in knows to fetch it again.

UserChange.description:
UserChange is one user a partner should re-read - or, when Type is
UserChangeDeleted, stop holding altogether.

renewed.description:
Renewed is when the owner last confirmed the opportunity is still active. The
client needs it to know whether a confirmation is due, so that it only asks when
the batch renewal clock says so rather than on every visit.

abTestResponse.description: abTestResponse is the response for A/B test variant

aiImageRegenerateResponse.description: aiImageRegenerateResponse is the response after regenerating an AI image

aiImagesCountResponse.description: aiImagesCountResponse returns the count of images pending review

aiImagesReviewResponse.description: aiImagesReviewResponse is the list of AI images pending review

chatMessageCreatedResponse.description: chatMessageCreatedResponse is the response for creating a chat message

chatRoomCreatedResponse.description: chatRoomCreatedResponse is the response for creating/opening a chat room

fileResponse.description: fileResponse is the response for binary file data

genericResponse.description: genericResponse is a generic JSON response for endpoints returning fiber.Map

noContentResponse.description: noContentResponse is the response for 204 No Content

successResponse.description: successResponse is the response for successful operations
